$comment: Advisories that are KNOWN, ASSESSED and TEMPORARILY ACCEPTED.
An entry here waives ONE advisory id until its reviewBy date. Anything not
listed — or listed but past reviewBy — still fails the build.
Adding an entry requires: why it cannot be fixed, what the real exposure is,
and a date. Never add one just to make CI green.

exceptions.title: sharp inherited vulnerabilities in libvips
exceptions.reason: Transitive through next. No released Next version escapes the advisory range (9.3.4-canary.0 - 16.3.0-preview.7); we are already on latest (16.2.12). npm's only offered fix is next@9.3.3, a seven-major downgrade.
exceptions.exposure: Limited. sharp runs at build time over first-party art, and at runtime only for next/image fetches from the four hosts in remotePatterns. No user-supplied image ever reaches it.

exceptions.title: Arbitrary file read via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL
exceptions.reason: Bundled inside next. Same story: not separately upgradable.
exceptions.exposure: None at runtime. postcss runs at build time over our own CSS; no attacker-controlled stylesheet exists in the pipeline.

exceptions.title: Path traversal in previous source map auto-loading
exceptions.reason: Bundled inside next. Not separately upgradable.
exceptions.exposure: None at runtime. Build-time only, over our own CSS.

$comment: The four `next` advisories are NOT waived and NOT exploitable here — they
are recorded so the assessment is not lost:
- middleware/proxy bypass: no middleware.ts exists in the repo.
- SSRF in Server Actions: no 'use server' anywhere in the tree.
- SSRF in rewrites: we declare redirects() only, from a static array in
lib/redirects. No rewrites, no request-derived destinations.
- Image Optimization DoS via SVG: dangerouslyAllowSVG is not set and
remotePatterns is four fixed hosts. Reachable in principle; the one to
re-check first when a patched Next ships.
